audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Ziggs 'short-range' and 'short-ranged'.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb 850, Hexplosive Minefield 900, Satchel Charge 1000, Mega Inferno Bomb 5000 — against Pillar of Flame's 900 and Sear's 1050 that is not a range deficit, and it is the premise most of the lane advice was resting on.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the affected spikes and prose around real ranges and cooldowns. I did NOT move the level chart — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid all claimed Pyroclasm out-ranges Mega Inferno Bomb.
audit.why: Pyroclasm is 750 range; Mega Inferno Bomb is 5000. It is off by more than six times, and it tells a player to try to win a poke war he cannot enter.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten: you never out-range his R, so the level 6 plan is to close inside 750 with Blaze already applied.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said Satchel Charge deals percent health, and nothing mentioned Short Fuse.
audit.why: _missing flags resistances-invalidated (Satchel Charge) and autoreset-burst-tell (Short Fuse): stacking MR is the wrong answer, and his opening tell is the empowered auto, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Percent-health and the 20s displacement now in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and dontsFull[2].d; Short Fuse now drives spikes[0].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit, and dosFull[2].d asserted a 'fifteen-second' Satchel Charge.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12 — fifteen is not a rank. Bouncing Bomb is 6s at rank 1, Hexplosive Minefield a flat 16s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120/95/70.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in both fields plus dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text and wants.foe[1] described a 'ward-hop' / 'W ward-jump'.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Satchel Charge a self-knockback — Ziggs is knocked away and takes no damage. Nothing in the kit involves a ward, and naming a mechanic that does not exist reads as invented.
audit.corrected: Both restated as Satchel Charge self-displacement on a 20s cooldown.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - E-Q stun package is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge (W): 20s at rank 1, 12s maxed — it knocks him clear and deals percent health, so armour and MR do not answer it. He is catchable only while it is down. - Bouncing Bomb is 6s, Hexplosive Minefield a flat 16s.

edits.before: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Pillar of Flame lands after a delay at 900 — put it where he must stand to farm, not where he stands now.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Conflagration ablazes point-blank inside 625, and only an ablaze target gets stunned by Sear — that order never changes.

edits.before: Ziggs burns Satchel Charge on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Ziggs burns Satchel Charge on nothing and owes you 20 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: That’s Ziggs’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Unablazed, Sear is 70 mana and 8 seconds spent for no stun and no trade.

edits.before: Your stun only exists on ablaze targets — a Q thrown at a clean health bar is the most expensive miss in your kit.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is 6s at rank 1 against your 10s pillar — stepping out during that gap is how the poke war is lost.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Satchel Charge knocks him clear of your rotation for 20s at rank 1 — spend the full package only once that displacement is gone.

edits.before: Track Ziggs’s Satchel Charge: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Satchel Charge: 20s at rank 1, it knocks him away, and it deals percent health, so stacking resistances answers nothing.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by out-poking you with Bouncing Bomb on 6s, then Satchel-charging out of every rotation you commit.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by closing the distance he cannot hold — Satchel Charge is his only displacement, and while it is down he has no escape.

edits.before: If Ziggs opens the score, reset expectations and respect Satchel Charge doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W-E clears and stay relevant through stun-burn peel.
edits.after: If Ziggs opens the score his Short Fuse and Bouncing Bomb chip you off every wave — farm from behind the pillar, never step up while Satchel Charge is up, and stay useful as stun-burn peel in fights.

edits.before: Your Pyroclasm out-ranges his ult in a real skirmish, letting you win contested fights.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 — you never out-range it, so win by closing to your 750.

edits.before: Once you hit level 3 with Q+E both up, your poke pattern starts trading roughly even into Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb, but he still edges you out at level 1-2 since his auto-attack range plus Q harass punishes your melee-range minion clears before your own zoning is online.
edits.after: Once you hit level 3 with W and E both up, your poke trades roughly even into Bouncing Bomb, but he edges you at levels 1-2: Short Fuse makes his next auto hurt and his Q is 6s at rank 1 against your 10s pillar, so he chips you before your zoning is online.

edits.before: Your Pyroclasm bounces reach further into his backline positioning than his own Mega Inferno Bomb can threaten you from, letting you close the poke gap and start winning skirmishes around objectives.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb throws 5000 units, so Pyroclasm never out-ranges it. Level 6 is about the opposite: get inside 750 with Blaze already on him, where his only escape is a Satchel Charge on 20 seconds.

edits.before: Luden's/Liandry's burst gives you a two-item spike where your combo threatens to kill him outright if he ever misplaces a ward-hop or gets caught pushing, something his short-range kit can't punish back.
edits.after: Liandry's burst gives you a spike where the full rotation threatens to kill him outright if he is caught with Satchel Charge down — his only displacement, and 20 seconds at rank 1 once he spends it on the wave.

edits.before: Your AoE burst and Conflagration DoT out-trade his siege-oriented kit in real fights since he has to actually hit skillshots on you while your zone denial punishes him for standing near minions at all.
edits.after: Your AoE burst and the Blaze burn out-trade his siege kit in a real fight, since every spell he owns is a skillshot he has to land while a pillar under the wave punishes him for standing near it at all.

edits.before: From level 3 onward your stun-into-burst combo out-trades his single-target Q poke, and by 6 your Pyroclasm threatens further than his ult can safely punish, letting you contest skirmishes and objectives where before you had to play passive. He's forced into a support role hitting siege waves rather than fighting you directly in lane.
edits.after: From level 3 onward your ablaze-into-Sear combo out-trades his Bouncing Bomb poke, and by 6 the fight you want is inside 750, where Pyroclasm bounces and his only escape is a 20-second Satchel Charge. Never try to out-range Mega Inferno Bomb; it throws 5000 units and will always reach the wave you are standing in.

edits.before: With Luden's or Liandry's online you can delete him in one rotation if he ever misplaces positioning, and his short-ranged, skillshot-reliant kit just can't keep up with your zone denial and burst in a straight fight — he has to rely entirely on hitting you from max range on cooldown, which isn't reliable enough to offset your item spike.
edits.after: With Luden's or Liandry's online you can delete him in one rotation if he is ever caught with Satchel Charge down, and every spell he owns is a skillshot he has to land while Blaze is already ticking on him. He can still throw Mega Inferno Bomb from 5000 units on a 70-second cooldown, so the fight you want is the one where he has spent it.

edits.before: Play patient at levels 1-2 and just farm safely with auto-attacks under his poke
edits.after: Farm patiently at levels 1-2; his Bouncing Bomb is 6s against your 10s pillar

edits.before: Look to all-in the instant you hit level 3 with Q and E both available
edits.after: All-in at level 3 with W and E up — ablaze first, then Sear stuns

edits.before: Use W ward-jump to extend Q range safely and deny approach
edits.after: Use Satchel Charge to knock himself clear of Brand's rotation

notes: MC_REAL_GAMES gives 314 games, so this matchup is audited rather than deferred. LEVEL CHART LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: the packet flags it as contradicting the data (46.18% win rate against a chart giving Brand 6 of 7 rows), but the two layers disagree in a way I cannot resolve from the kits — full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' with diff EVEN, while content win[] reads Ziggs then Brand six times. Three sources give three answers (46.18% says Ziggs, the full layer says even, the content layer says Brand), so per the chart rule I moved nothing and raised it in questionsForUser. Everything else in this proposal is prose grounded in the kit.
